title: Brief Addiction Monitor (BAM)
formula:
The BAM score is calculated by the addition of the selected points. Please ask your patient:

| Question | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. In the past 30 days, how would you say your physical health has been? | Excellent | 0 |
| Very good | 1 | |
| Good | 2 | |
| Fair | 3 | |
| Poor | 4 | |
| 2. In the past 30 days, how many nights did you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 3. In the past 30 days, how many days have you felt depressed, anxious, angry, or very upset throughout most of the day? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 4. In the past 30 days, how many days did you drink ANY alcohol? | 0 (skip to #6) | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 5. In the past 30 days, how many days did you have at least 5 drinks (if you are a man) or at least 4 drinks (if you are a woman)? *One drink is considered one shot of hard liquor (1.5 ounce) or 12 ounce can/bottle of beer or 5 ounce glass of wine. | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 6. In the past 30 days, how many days did you use any illegal/street drugs or abuse any prescription medications? | 0 (skip to #8) | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 7. In the past 30 days, how many days did you use any of the following drugs: | | |
| 7A. Marijuana (cannabis, pot, weed)? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 7B. Sedatives/tranquilizers (e.g., “benzos,” Valium, Xanax, Ativan, Ambien, “barbs,” phenobarbital, downers, etc.)? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 7C. Cocaine/crack? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 7D. Other stimulants (e.g., amphetamine, methamphetamine, Dexedrine, Ritalin, Adderall, “speed,” "crystal meth," “ice,” etc.)? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 7E. Opiates (e.g., heroin, morphine, Dilaudid, Demerol, Oxycontin, "oxy," codeine (tylenol 2,3,4), Percocet, Vicodin, fentanyl, etc.)? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 7F. Inhalants (glues/adhesives, nail polish remover, paint thinner, etc.)? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 7G. Other drugs (steroids, non-prescription sleep/diet pills, Benadryl, ephedra, other over-the-counter/unknown medications)? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 8. In the past 30 days, how much were you bothered by cravings or urges to drink alcohol or use drugs? | Not at all | 0 |
| Slightly | 1 | |
| Moderately | 2 | |
| Considerably | 3 | |
| Extremely | 4 | |
| 9. How confident are you in your ability to be completely abstinent (clean) from alcohol and drugs in the next 30 days? | Not at all | 0 |
| Slightly | 1 | |
| Moderately | 2 | |
| Considerably | 3 | |
| Extremely | 4 | |
| 10. In the past 30 days, how many days did you attend self-help meetings like AA or NA to support your recovery? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 11. In the past 30 days, how many days were you in any situations or with any people that might put you at an increased risk for using alcohol or drugs (i.e., around risky “people, places, or things”)? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 12. Does your religion or spirituality help support your recovery? | Not at all | 0 |
| Slightly | 1 | |
| Moderately | 2 | |
| Considerably | 3 | |
| Extremely | 4 | |
| 13. In the past 30 days, how many days did you spend much of the time at work, school, or doing volunteer work? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 14. Do you have enough income (from legal sources) to pay for necessities such as housing, transportation, food, and clothing for yourself and your dependents? | No | 0 |
| Yes | 4 | |
| 15. In the past 30 days, how much have you been bothered by arguments or had problems getting along with any family members or friends? | Not at all | 0 |
| Slightly | 1 | |
| Moderately | 2 | |
| Considerably | 3 | |
| Extremely | 4 | |
| 16. In the past 30 days, how many days were you in contact or spent time with any family members or friends who are supportive of your recovery? | 0 | 0 |
| 1-3 | 1 | |
| 4-8 | 2 | |
| 9-15 | 3 | |
| 16-30 | 4 | |
| 17. How satisfied are you with your progress toward achieving your recovery goals? | Not at all | 0 |
| Slightly | 1 | |
| Moderately | 2 | |
| Considerably | 3 | |
| Extremely | 4 | |

how_to_use.why:
- Fournit une méthode standardisée pour évaluer et suivre la consommation de substances et les comportements associés.
- Facilite une documentation cohérente et le suivi de la progression des patients tout au long du traitement de la consommation de substances.
- Fournit des données pour guider des décisions thérapeutiques personnalisées dans le but d’améliorer les résultats du traitement.
- Comparé à d’autres outils apparentés, conçu pour être bref tout en offrant une couverture multidimensionnelle des domaines liés à l’addiction.
how_to_use.when:
- Can be used to assess the severity of a patient’s substance use and monitor progress during treatment.
- Useful in both inpatient and outpatient treatment settings.
- May be administered in-person in the clinical setting or self-administered at home prior to treatment appointments.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Élaboré et utilisé par le Département des Anciens Combattants des États-Unis (VA).
- Évalue plusieurs domaines, notamment les facteurs de risque de rechute ou d’aggravation de la sévérité de l’addiction, les facteurs protecteurs pour la sobriété, ainsi que la consommation de drogues et d’alcool.
- Peut être auto-administré ou administré par un clinicien.
- Les études de validation indiquent que l’outil est sensible au changement dans le temps.
- Les réponses peuvent être influencées par des événements récents plutôt que par des schémas à long terme.
- N’est pas destiné à être un outil diagnostique pour le trouble d’usage de substances.

next_steps.advice:
- Si l'on constate une absence de progression des scores, identifier des cibles thérapeutiques potentielles et ajuster le plan de soins en conséquence.
- Des améliorations significatives des scores au fil du temps peuvent orienter les décisions d'allègement des soins, lorsque cela est cliniquement approprié.
next_steps.management:
While the three factor scores can aid in informing severity and progress, examining individual item scores may be the most clinically useful to identify specific areas for intervention. Examples may include:

- Ensuring adequate primary care to optimize general physical health.
- Referring for mental health treatment.
- Referring for substance use specialty care.
- Managing cravings (e.g., with naltrexone).
- Providing case management to ensure access to care.
- Connecting with network social support systems.

more_info:
The three subscales include:

| Subscale | Question Number |
| --- | --- |
| Use factors | Any alcohol use (#4) |
| Heavy alcohol use (#5) | |
| Any drug use (#6) | |
| Risk factors | Physical health (#1) |
| Sleep (#2) | |
| Mood (#3) | |
| Cravings (#8) | |
| Risky situations (#11) | |
| Family/social problems (#15) | |
| Protective factors | Self-efficacy (#9) |
| Self-help behaviors (#10) | |
| Religion/spirituality (#12) | |
| Work/school participation (#13) | |
| Adequate income (#14) | |
| Sober support (#16) | |
